newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd seen still in red in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd seen still in red in Q1.

text.p: Dutch shipping and transport group Koninklijke Nedlloyd is expected to remain in the red in the first quarter of 1997 as the going remained tough for the company's container shipping activities.

Analysts forecast a wide range of first quarter results from a 44 million guilder loss to a nine million guilder profit, but most predicted a negative result, with a consensus loss of 17 million guilders. The results are due on Wednesday.
Last year, the company posted a loss of 15 million guilders in the first quarter, although this included a 30 million guilder book profit from ship sales.
The pressure again comes from Nedlloyd's ocean shipping operations, now part of P&O Nedlloyd Containers, the company's joint venture with Britain's Peninsular and Orient Steam Navigation Company.
"The company has already announced the volumes in container shipping would be weak... and rates (on average) seem to have been 10 percent lower," said Thibaud de Guerre of ING Barings.
The company is in the process of cutting costs. On Thursday, P&O chairman Lord Sterling said that the company was on track to realise cost savings of $200 million per year.
However, analysts say the savings will not affect the bottom line until at least the second quarter, and more likely, the third.
Some improvement may at least have occurred in Nedlloyd's land activities, grouped together as European Transport and Distribution.
"It looks like they'll probably have turned around the German side and possibly Van Gend and Loos will have improved," said Oscar Poos of Paribas.
Van Gend and Loos is Nedlloyd's main distribution arm in the Benelux countries.
